tasks.short: Gather the referral, medical background and earlier results, score the speech and language tests, evaluate everything to diagnose, plan treatment, and discuss the diagnosis with the client or parents.

steps.what: Speech therapist gathers the referral letter, medical background and earlier test results
Speech therapist scores speech and language test results with norm tables
Speech therapist evaluates test results and background information to diagnose the disorder
Speech therapist plans treatment for the speech, language or swallowing disorder
Speech therapist discusses the diagnosis with the client or parents

tasks.design: Referral letters and earlier results arrive in the practice's client record ({OTHER}) through the regional referral exchange instead of by e-mail. Raw test scores are entered in digital scoring that looks up norm scores, so norm tables are not read by hand. Diagnosing and planning treatment stay with the therapist; no software diagnoses.
tasks.previous_blocker: Letters came by e-mail or post and norm scores were looked up in printed tables.
tasks.enabler_now: Client records take referrals electronically; digital scoring computes norm scores.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed disorders do not fit one test.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that a child's stutter changes with who is in the room.

evidence.claim: Digital test scoring can compute norm scores from raw scores.
Solely automated care decisions need an article 22(2) basis; here the therapist diagnoses.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the diagnosis explained; treatment sessions are outside.
Input contract: referrals through the regional exchange; test publishers' scoring licences; fallback is e-mail and printed tables.
Diagnosing and planning do not change.

incremental.description: Speech therapist checks digital norm scores against the test manual at first use.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few new clients; high: a practice with many assessments.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write session notes, write evaluation and progress reports, send reports to the referring physician, register treatments for billing, check the claims, submit them to insurers, and keep the caseload overview.

steps.what: Speech therapist writes session notes after each treatment

loop.input: The recording of the session, made with the client's consent.
loop.output: A draft session note in SOEP format.
loop.check: A validator flags any test score not in the record and any statement on risk; the therapist reads, corrects and approves every note.
loop.stop: One draft per session; if the therapist rejects it, they write the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Typing from memory is the work being cut; a template still needs the session described in prose.

steps.what: Speech therapist writes reports on initial evaluation, progress and discharge

loop.input: The session notes, goals and test scores of the period.
loop.output: A draft evaluation, progress or discharge report.
loop.check: Code checks every score and date in the text matches the record; the therapist edits and approves.
loop.stop: Stops when the checks pass and the therapist approves, or after two failed redrafts the therapist writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reports explain progress in prose for physicians and parents; a template only lists scores.

steps.what: Speech therapist e-mails the report to the referring physician
Speech therapist registers treatments for billing records
Speech therapist checks the claims list
Speech therapist submits claims to health insurers
Speech therapist maintains the caseload overview in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: With the client's consent, a scribe ({OTHER}) drafts the session note from the recording into the client record; the therapist corrects and approves every note. Progress and discharge reports are drafted from notes and scores, with code checking every number; once approved they go to the referring physician through the secure exchange. Treatments booked in the agenda become claim lines, and after the therapist checks the list, claims go to insurers. The caseload overview is a view in the record instead of a spreadsheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes and reports were typed after hours and claims entered line by line.
tasks.enabler_now: Medical scribes draft notes into Dutch care records; practice systems turn agenda items into claims.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can contain errors, and some clients do not want recording.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a discharge report a parent can understand and a physician can use.
tasks.altitude: The therapist checks drafts and claim lists instead of typing them.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation; the clinician validates and the note goes into the care record.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians using Tandem notes self-estimated time per note falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes.
The IGJ holds providers responsible for careful use of generative AI, including checking whether it is a medical device.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session held to the caseload overview; insurer decisions are outside.
Input contract: recordings only with consent; agenda and claim codes in the practice system; fallback is typing and manual claims.
The therapist approves every note and report.
research_questions: How much does the therapist change in drafted notes?

already_counted.description: Speech therapist reads and corrects drafted notes.

incremental.description: Speech therapist asks consent for recording and notes it.

approvals.approved_version: The report as edited and approved by the therapist in s2.
The claims list as checked by the therapist in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many clients decline recording; high: most sessions recorded and claims from the agenda.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe and measure progress in sessions, compare it with the goals, decide treatment adjustments, and update the treatment plan and home exercises.

steps.what: Speech therapist monitors patients' progress during sessions
Speech therapist compares progress with the treatment goals in the file
Speech therapist decides how to adjust treatments
Speech therapist updates the treatment plan and home exercises

tasks.design: Goal scores per session go into the client record ({OTHER}), which shows progress per goal over time, so the therapist does not page back through notes. Home exercises come from an exercise library and are shared with the client in the client portal. Observing, deciding and adjusting treatment stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress had to be read from free-text notes and exercises were copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Client records show goal scores over time; exercise libraries can be shared through portals.
tasks.still_hard: Progress in voice or fluency varies from day to day.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a client needs a break, not harder exercises.

evidence.claim: Client records can chart goal scores over time; exercise libraries can be shared through portals.

assumptions: Boundary: from the treatment plan to the updated plan; discharge is outside.
Input contract: goal scores entered per session; fallback is free-text notes.
Observing and deciding do not change.
Clients open exercises in the portal in about the time a paper sheet took; no added client time.
research_questions: Do clients practise more at home?

incremental.description: Speech therapist enters a goal score after each session.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few goals per client; high: many clients with several goals.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the recommendations of physicians and psychologists, develop the treatment plan with goals, discuss it with the client or parents, implement treatment in sessions, and prepare home exercise materials.

steps.what: Speech therapist reads recommendations of physicians, psychologists and other professionals
Speech therapist develops treatment plans for problems such as stuttering, delayed language or swallowing disorders
Speech therapist discusses the plan with the client or parents
Speech therapist implements the treatment plan in sessions
Speech therapist prepares home exercise materials

tasks.design: Letters from physicians and psychologists arrive in the client record ({OTHER}) through the secure exchange. Treatment plans start from a goal library per disorder that the therapist picks from and adapts. Home exercises come from the practice's exercise library. Developing the plan, agreeing it and treating stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Letters came by post or e-mail and plans were written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Client records take letters electronically; goal libraries are common in practice systems.
tasks.still_hard: Every client's mix of problems is different.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the exercise a shy child will actually do.

evidence.claim: Practice systems offer goal libraries and electronic receipt of letters.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to exercise materials; discharge is outside.
Input contract: letters through the secure exchange; goal library kept by the practice; fallback is post and writing from scratch.
Developing, agreeing and treating do not change.
research_questions: Do plans get written sooner after referral?

incremental.description: Speech therapist keeps the goal library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few new plans; high: many new clients each month.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The speech therapist keeps diagnosing, planning and treating; typed notes and reports, norm tables and claim entry shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A therapist with more time for treatment.
